headline: High-risk git/workspace conflict and prompt-injection exposure: Aider can write shared repo state while RisingWave is undocumented, so pairwise safety is uncertain and defaults are unsafe.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a git repo, so attacker-controlled content in the workspace can influence its prompts or edits. RisingWave has no documented interactive parsing surface, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout, injected text in files can be surfaced to Aider's prompt context.
IF RisingWave outputs repository content that Aider later reads, that content can steer subsequent edits.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different working copies.
Require manual review of any file content before Aider consumes it.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted repo text where possible.
Use a staging branch for Aider edits.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for content passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress to configured model providers, while RisingWave is documented as network-egress none. The shared-repo path can still expose code or history to Aider's backend, but the blast radius is limited to repository data rather than broader secrets, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the shared repository contains secrets or proprietary source, Aider may transmit them to configured model providers.
IF RisingWave and Aider share the same checkout, file contents visible to Aider can leave the local environment via Aider's backend calls.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared repo before use.
Use a redacted branch for Aider.
Restrict Aider to a local-only model provider if available.
Audit git history for sensitive blobs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via a shared git repo. RisingWave has no documented locking or write controls here, so concurrent edits to the same repo can race and corrupt git state or overwrite work; uncertainty does not justify lowering severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git working tree, commits or file edits can conflict.
IF either agent modifies the same branch without external locking, one agent can overwrite the other's changes.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Review and merge changes manually.
Pause one agent while the other commits.
requires-engineering: add repository-level optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes and git commits, and RisingWave is a data-engineering system that may consume or depend on those outputs in a pipeline. Because no verification or handoff protocol is documented for the pair, Aider's output could be treated as authoritative by downstream RisingWave workflows, but the direct action blast radius is not established.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests artifacts produced by Aider without validation, incorrect code or configs can propagate downstream.
IF Aider commits a faulty change that RisingWave later deploys or processes, the error can cascade into multiple work products.
mitigations: Require a human review gate before downstream use.
Add tests for any Aider-produced artifact.
Pin inputs to known-good versions.
Roll back immediately on failed validation.
requires-engineering: implement schema and semantic validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles model-provider API keys and source code/git history, but RisingWave has no documented compliance or residency surface in the profile. With only one side documented, the pairwise compliance risk is limited to a possible policy mismatch rather than a proven breach, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF the shared repository contains regulated data, Aider's provider calls may create a policy mismatch.
IF organizational policy forbids source-code egress to third-party model providers, using Aider violates that policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Use an approved local model for Aider.
Review data-handling policy before pairing.
Limit logs and retention on the Aider side.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both agents.
